questions.question: A student in Charleston is a citizen of both the United States and West Virginia. That is because in the American system:
questions.correctAnswer: Citizenship operates at two levels at once - national citizenship and state citizenship
distractors: State citizenship replaces national citizenship inside state borders
Only people born in a state capital hold state citizenship
Citizenship is granted by county governments
questions.explanation: The Fourteenth Amendment and the state constitutions work together: a person born or naturalized in the United States is a citizen of the nation and of the state where they live, with rights and duties at both levels.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Two levels, one citizen: nation and state.

img.tip: T-Rexy says: Two levels, one citizen: nation and state.
img.title: CITIZEN AT TWO LEVELS

questions.question: The rights of West Virginia citizens - speech, religion, due process and more - are listed in which part of the West Virginia Constitution?
questions.correctAnswer: Article III, the Declaration of Rights
distractors: The Preamble
The article creating the Legislature
The schedule of county boundaries
questions.explanation: West Virginia places its bill of rights near the front of its constitution as Article III, the Declaration of Rights - the state counterpart to the Bill of Rights in the United States Constitution, and sometimes broader than it.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Article III declares the rights.

questions.question: Which level of government is mainly responsible for the county roads, local schools and sheriff's patrols a West Virginia family uses every week?
questions.correctAnswer: Local government - the county and any city or town government
distractors: The federal government in Washington
The Supreme Court of Appeals
The state Senate acting alone
questions.explanation: Counties and municipalities deliver the services closest to daily life: roads, schools through county boards of education, water, and law enforcement. State and federal governments set wider policy and funding, but the county commission and city hall do the local work.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Closest government does the daily work.

questions.question: Before the West Virginia Constitution can be amended, a proposed amendment must first be approved by:
questions.correctAnswer: A two-thirds vote in each house of the West Virginia Legislature
distractors: A simple majority in one house only
The governor acting alone
A ruling of the Supreme Court of Appeals
questions.explanation: Article XIV of the state constitution sets a two-step road: two-thirds of all members elected to each house must agree to propose the amendment, and then the voters themselves decide it at an election. Neither step alone is enough.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Two-thirds propose - the people decide.

img.scene: A grand legislative chamber with two curved banks of empty desks and flags at the front, symbolic and wide. No readable text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: T-Rexy says: Two-thirds propose - the people decide.
img.title: HOW AMENDMENTS BEGIN

questions.question: A proposed amendment to the West Virginia Constitution has passed the Legislature by the required vote. What must happen next for it to take effect?
questions.correctAnswer: A majority of West Virginia voters must approve it at an election
distractors: The governor must sign it like an ordinary bill
It takes effect automatically after 30 days
Each county commission must ratify it separately
questions.explanation: Unlike an ordinary law, a constitutional amendment is not signed or vetoed by the governor. Once the Legislature proposes it, the amendment goes on the ballot and becomes part of the constitution only if the voters approve it.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: The ballot box finishes an amendment.

questions.question: A West Virginian is told she has no right to a jury trial because the case is a state case. Why is that wrong under the state constitution?
questions.correctAnswer: Article III's Declaration of Rights guarantees jury trial and due process in West Virginia courts, not only in federal ones
distractors: The state constitution copies federal court rules word for word
Jury trials exist in West Virginia only by custom, not by right
The governor grants jury trials case by case
questions.explanation: The Declaration of Rights in Article III protects West Virginians directly: it covers due process of law, jury trial, speech, religion, and protection against unreasonable searches. A state case is still bound by those state guarantees.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: State rights protect you in state court too.

img.tip: T-Rexy says: State rights protect you in state court too.
img.title: RIGHTS IN STATE COURT

questions.question: Which of these is a duty of citizenship in West Virginia rather than a right?
questions.correctAnswer: Serving on a jury when lawfully called
distractors: Speaking freely about public issues
Practicing a religion of one's choice
Petitioning the government
questions.explanation: Rights are protections the government must respect; duties are obligations citizenship carries. Jury service, obeying the law, paying taxes and (for young citizens) attending school are duties - speech, religion and petition are rights.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Rights protect you; duties ask of you.

questions.question: An amendment is approved by two-thirds of the Senate but only a bare majority of the House of Delegates. What is the result?
questions.correctAnswer: The amendment fails - both houses must reach two-thirds of all members elected
distractors: It passes, because the Senate vote controls
It passes if the governor certifies it
It goes to the voters anyway as an advisory question
questions.explanation: Article XIV requires two-thirds of all the members elected to EACH house. A shortfall in either chamber ends the proposal for that session, no matter how large the other chamber's vote was.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Two-thirds means both houses, every time.

img.tip: T-Rexy says: Two-thirds means both houses, every time.

questions.question: Why has the West Virginia Constitution of 1872 been amended many more times than the United States Constitution?
questions.correctAnswer: It is much more detailed - covering topics like education, taxation and counties - and its amendment path, while strict, is completed more often than the federal one
distractors: Amendments to it need no voter approval
The federal constitution cannot be amended at all
West Virginia amendments are written by the courts
questions.explanation: State constitutions do the detailed housekeeping of government, so they run long and change as needs change. West Virginia voters have approved well over a hundred amendments since 1872, against 27 amendments to the far shorter federal frame since 1789.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: A detailed constitution changes more often.

questions.question: A county official argues a state rule is unfair and simply refuses to follow the West Virginia Constitution in his county. Which principle answers him?
questions.correctAnswer: The state constitution is the highest law within West Virginia - no county or official may set it aside; change must come by amendment
distractors: Counties may suspend state rules for one year
Home rule lets each county rewrite the constitution locally
Officials may ignore any rule they did not vote for
questions.explanation: Within state matters, the West Virginia Constitution outranks statutes, county ordinances and official preferences alike. The lawful remedy for a bad provision is the Article XIV amendment process - proposal by the Legislature and approval by the voters.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Amend it lawfully - never just ignore it.

img.tip: T-Rexy says: Amend it lawfully - never just ignore it.

questions.question: The lawmaking branch of West Virginia government is the Legislature, which is made up of:
questions.correctAnswer: The Senate and the House of Delegates
distractors: The governor and the cabinet
The circuit courts and magistrate courts
The county commissions acting together
questions.explanation: Like Congress, the West Virginia Legislature is bicameral: a Senate and a House of Delegates, both meeting at the Capitol in Charleston during the annual regular session. West Virginia is unlike Nebraska, whose legislature has only one house.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Two houses in Charleston make the laws.

questions.question: In West Virginia government, the executive branch - headed by the governor - is chiefly responsible for:
questions.correctAnswer: Carrying out and enforcing the laws the Legislature passes
distractors: Writing the laws itself
Deciding court cases
Counting the votes in elections
questions.explanation: The three branches divide the work: the Legislature makes laws, the governor and the executive agencies enforce them, and the courts interpret them when disputes arise. The governor also proposes a budget and can sign or veto bills.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Legislature writes it; governor runs it.

questions.question: The highest court in West Virginia, the court of last resort for state-law questions, is:
questions.correctAnswer: The Supreme Court of Appeals of West Virginia
distractors: The Kanawha County Circuit Court
The Legislature's judiciary committee
The United States District Court
questions.explanation: Five justices sit on the Supreme Court of Appeals in Charleston. Below it, circuit courts hear the major trials, and its decisions on West Virginia law are final unless a federal question takes a case into the federal system.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Five justices sit at the top.

questions.question: How many members serve in the West Virginia Senate?
questions.correctAnswer: 34 senators, elected from senatorial districts across the state
distractors: 17 senators, one per congressional district
50 senators, matching the state count of the U.S. Senate
100 senators, the same as the House of Delegates
questions.explanation: The Senate is the smaller chamber: 34 members serving four-year staggered terms. The size difference matters - a bill must win over two differently sized and differently elected chambers before it can become law.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: The smaller chamber holds thirty-four.

questions.question: How many members serve in the West Virginia House of Delegates?
questions.correctAnswer: 100 delegates, elected every two years
distractors: 34 delegates, matching the Senate
67 delegates, one for each judicial circuit
150 delegates, the largest chamber in America
questions.explanation: The House of Delegates is the larger, more frequently elected chamber: 100 members on two-year terms, which keeps it closely tied to current public opinion. Together the two chambers total 134 legislators.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: One hundred delegates, elected every two years.

questions.question: A felony criminal case and a lawsuit over a large sum of money in West Virginia are heard first in:
questions.correctAnswer: Circuit court - the state's general trial courts
distractors: Magistrate court
Family court
The Supreme Court of Appeals
questions.explanation: Circuit courts are West Virginia's courts of general jurisdiction: serious criminal cases, major civil suits, and appeals from the lower courts. Each circuit covers one or more counties, and circuit judges are elected by the voters of the circuit.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Big cases start in circuit court.

questions.question: Magistrate courts in West Virginia handle which kinds of matters?
questions.correctAnswer: Misdemeanors, preliminary hearings in felony cases, and small civil claims
distractors: Only appeals from the Supreme Court
Divorce and child custody decrees
Constitutional amendments
questions.explanation: Magistrates are the front door of the court system: they issue warrants, conduct preliminary hearings, try misdemeanors, and hear small claims. Their work keeps minor matters moving quickly so circuit courts can focus on major cases.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Magistrates handle the front door of justice.

questions.question: Divorce, child custody and child support cases in West Virginia are decided in:
questions.correctAnswer: Family court, whose judges specialize in domestic matters
distractors: Magistrate court
The governor's office
A jury of county commissioners
questions.explanation: West Virginia created family courts so that sensitive household cases - divorce, custody, support, visitation and domestic protective matters - are heard by judges who handle that docket full time, with procedures designed around families.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Family cases go to family court.

questions.question: A road-funding bill clears both houses in Charleston, but the governor vetoes it. Under the state constitution, lawmakers can still enact it if they:
questions.correctAnswer: Repass it with a majority of the members elected to each house voting to override
distractors: Repass it by a two-thirds vote, exactly like Congress
Accept the veto - a West Virginia veto is final
Ask the Supreme Court of Appeals to sign it
questions.explanation: West Virginia's override rule is easier to reach than the federal one: the Constitution requires only a majority of the members elected to each house (for most bills) to override a veto, where Congress needs two-thirds. The difference is a favorite point of comparison between the two constitutions.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: In West Virginia, a majority can override.

img.tip: T-Rexy says: In West Virginia, a majority can override.

questions.question: How do West Virginians choose the justices of their Supreme Court of Appeals?
questions.correctAnswer: Justices are elected by the voters in nonpartisan elections to twelve-year terms
distractors: The governor appoints them for life
The Senate confirms presidential nominees
County commissions select them by rotation
questions.explanation: Unlike the appointed-for-life justices of the United States Supreme Court, West Virginia justices face the voters: they are elected statewide in nonpartisan elections - no party labels on the ballot - for long twelve-year terms meant to balance accountability with independence.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Elected, nonpartisan, twelve-year terms.

questions.question: West Virginia's general election - when voters choose state and national officials - is held:
questions.correctAnswer: In November of even-numbered years
distractors: Every spring, in April
Only when the governor calls one
In November of odd-numbered years
questions.explanation: The general election falls on the Tuesday after the first Monday in November in even years, matching the national rhythm: presidential elections every four years and midterm elections between them.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: November, even years: the general election.

questions.question: What is the main job of a primary election in West Virginia?
questions.correctAnswer: Each political party chooses the nominees who will represent it in the general election
distractors: Voters amend the state constitution
The Legislature elects the governor
Counties set their tax rates
questions.explanation: West Virginia holds its primary in May. Candidates of the same party compete for the nomination; the winners carry their party's banner into November, where voters make the final choice between the parties' nominees.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: May narrows the field; November decides.

questions.question: West Virginia voters are called to the polls in March for a special election. Special elections exist to:
questions.correctAnswer: Decide a single urgent question - filling a vacancy or approving a levy or bond - outside the regular cycle
distractors: Replace the general election every four years
Elect magistrates only
Rehearse new voting machines
questions.explanation: A special election handles business that cannot wait for the next regular election: a sudden vacancy in office, or voter approval of a school levy or a bond issue. The same democratic machinery runs, focused on one decision.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: One urgent question, one special vote.

questions.question: The governing body of a West Virginia county - the body that sets the county budget and oversees county services - is:
questions.correctAnswer: The county commission
distractors: The board of education
The circuit court
The sheriff's department
questions.explanation: Each of West Virginia's counties is governed by an elected county commission, usually of three commissioners. Separately elected officials - sheriff, clerk, assessor, prosecuting attorney - run their own offices, and the board of education runs the schools.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Three commissioners run the county.

47 counties
63 counties

questions.question: The natural resource that has shaped West Virginia's economy more than any other for over a century is:
questions.correctAnswer: Coal
distractors: Cotton
Copper
Cranberries
questions.explanation: Bituminous coal from the Appalachian coalfields powered American industry, railroads and electricity. It built towns, railroads and fortunes in West Virginia - and its booms and declines have driven the state's economy ever since the late 1800s.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Coal built the modern state.

questions.question: A severance tax, one of West Virginia's important revenue sources, is:
questions.correctAnswer: A tax collected when natural resources such as coal, oil and natural gas are extracted (severed) from the ground
distractors: A tax on severing diplomatic relations
A fee for cutting timber for firewood only
A penalty employers pay when laying off workers
questions.explanation: Severance taxes turn one-time natural wealth into public revenue: when a ton of coal or a volume of gas leaves West Virginia ground, a share of its value funds state government and is shared back with producing counties and towns.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Severed from the ground, taxed for the public.

img.tip: T-Rexy says: Severed from the ground, taxed for the public.

questions.question: Why do economists watch severance tax collections closely in West Virginia?
questions.correctAnswer: Because they rise and fall with coal and gas prices, making a big share of the state budget rise and fall with energy markets
distractors: Because the tax is the state's only source of revenue
Because the governor sets the rate each week
Because counties refuse to spend the money
questions.explanation: Energy prices swing sharply, and severance revenue swings with them. In boom years the tax fills the treasury; in bust years budgets tighten statewide - a standing argument for saving windfalls and broadening the economy.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: When coal prices swing, budgets swing.

img.tip: T-Rexy says: When coal prices swing, budgets swing.

questions.question: In West Virginia history, 'absentee ownership' means:
questions.correctAnswer: Much of the state's land and mineral rights came to be owned by companies and people living outside West Virginia
distractors: Farmers who were absent from their fields at harvest
Students absent from school without an excuse
Counties owned by the federal government
questions.explanation: In the late 1800s and early 1900s, agents bought vast tracts of land and mineral rights cheaply from local families. The coal, timber and gas wealth then flowed largely to out-of-state owners, while the mining and cutting happened - and the costs landed - in West Virginia.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: The wealth left; the work stayed.

questions.question: Which statement best captures the trade-off historians debate about absentee ownership in West Virginia?
questions.correctAnswer: Outside owners brought the capital that built mines, railroads and jobs, but much of the profit left the state and local people had little control over the land's use
distractors: It brought only benefits and no costs
It brought only costs and no benefits
It ended all mining in the state
questions.explanation: Both halves are documented: without outside capital the coalfields would have developed far more slowly, yet severed mineral rights and distant decision-making limited local wealth and control for generations - a tension still visible in land records today.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Capital came in; control went out.

questions.question: Money from the West Virginia Lottery is dedicated by law mainly to support:

distractors: The governor's travel budget
Private gambling companies
Out-of-state highway projects
questions.explanation: Voters approved the lottery expecting public benefit: lottery profits are directed to education programs, senior citizen services, and tourism and parks - visible in school funding and senior centers across the state.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Lottery dollars flow to schools and seniors.

Driver licensing program
State income tax form

Choose a prom venue

Steel manufacturing
Commercial fishing

Chemistry is the only subject taught in its schools
The valley was named after a chemist governor
questions.explanation: Salt deposits, coal, natural gas and a navigable river gave chemical makers feedstocks, fuel and shipping in one place. From the early 1900s the valley produced chemicals used nationwide, including synthetic rubber and plastics materials in wartime.

questions.question: Northern West Virginia was once a national center of glassmaking. The industry grew there because the region offered:
questions.correctAnswer: Silica sand, cheap natural gas for furnaces, and river and rail transport
distractors: Ocean beaches for sand collection
